title: Games for Artificial Intelligence Research: A Review and Perspectives
extended_summary:
This paper surveys games and game-based platforms used for artificial intelligence research, with a focus on how different environments support AI methods for playing and designing games. It asks what kinds of games have been used as testbeds, how they are organized by game type and research purpose, and which environments are most suitable for different AI tasks such as planning, reinforcement learning, multi-agent coordination, procedural content generation, and game balancing.

The review covers publicly available tabletop games, video games, and multi-game platforms published or used in recent AI research, mainly from 2016 to February 2024. It categorizes environments by game genre, number of agents, observability, programming language, and whether they have associated competitions. The paper also discusses platforms for game design and content generation, including 2D and 3D level generation, narrative generation, rhythm chart generation, and card/board game generation. Although it mentions education in the context of games as testbeds, it does not report an empirical study involving learners or educators.

The main conclusion is that games remain valuable and increasingly diverse benchmarks for AI research, but different platforms serve different needs. The authors recommend specific environments for tasks such as RL, planning, generalization, multi-agent cooperation/competition, and procedural content generation. They also highlight persistent challenges in game AI, including high-dimensional representations, poor exploration, partial observability, generalization, and multi-agent complexity. The paper is primarily a taxonomy and guidance resource rather than an intervention study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative survey/review paper rather than an empirical study of K-12 learners or interventions. It does not use a clear experimental or quasi-experimental design to estimate outcomes, so it provides no direct evidence for learner effects in the target topic.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not evaluate any educational impact, learner subgroup effects, or K-12 outcomes. Its contribution is taxonomic and methodological for AI/game research, not an intervention effect estimate.

interventions.use_case: A review of games and game-based platforms used as AI testbeds, including board/card games, grid-based and 3D video games, and game-based environments for AI research and education.
